items.title: 砸錢拚算力 最後誰賺錢？避險基金投資長撰文示警AI獲利難題
items.title_en: Spending Big on Compute: Who Ultimately Profits? A Hedge Fund CIO Warns of AI Profit Challenges
paras: AI需求持續擴張，是否就代表模型開發商能長期獲取高額利潤？One River資產管理投資長彼得斯(Eric Peters)在一篇投資評論中，透過與投資人Sparks的對話提出另一種思考：隨著融資成本攀升，AI基礎建設熱潮可能面臨資金考驗，而最終受益最大的，未必是生產AI服務的公司，而是善用這些服務的企業。
文章中的Sparks是一名投資人與創業家。對於當前投資環境，他以「典型的景氣循環末期」形容，認為判斷行情能否延續，不能只看技術採用率與需求成長，也必須檢視支撐投資的資金流向，以及企業取得資本的成本。

融資成本攀升 市場可能從怕錯過轉為怕接盤

Sparks認為，大型投資循環進入後期時，金融交易往往變得更加複雜，風險也更難辨識。他以金融危機前的擔保債務憑證(CDO)及再證券化商品為例指出，越接近循環尾聲，最後發行的證券往往越複雜、越難理解，也越危險。
在他的分析中，轉折不一定始於需求崩跌，而可能先出現在融資條件轉差。當資金成本上升，部分原本勉強可行的投資案便不再划算，整體擴張速度也會隨之放緩。
對債券投資人而言，若既有持債價格下跌，新融資案又必須提供更高利率才能吸引資金，便會重新評估承擔風險的意願。資金供應轉趨保守，又可能進一步推高企業融資成本，形成相互強化的壓力。
「投資人會從害怕錯過，轉為害怕成為最後接手的人。」Sparks表示，這種轉變不會一夕完成，但等到警訊已經明顯到所有人都能察覺時，往往已錯過調整時機。
他認為，市場形成重大高點是一段過程，通常先由財務較弱的業者承受壓力，再逐步侵蝕支撐整體行情的基礎。不過，這是他對市場循環的判斷，並不代表股市轉折的時間已能確定。

AI需求不等於高利潤 模型業者恐更像公用事業

除了融資風險，文章另一個核心問題是：AI企業投入龐大資本建置算力後，究竟能形成具有定價能力的事業，還是陷入資本密集、利潤有限的競爭？
Sparks以亞馬遜(AMZN-US)為例指出，若扣除雲端服務AWS與廣告業務，其核心仍是零售與物流，而這類生意通常需要大量資本，利潤率也相對有限。相較之下，他認為Alphabet(GOOGL-US)旗下Google的市場地位與高利潤，更接近投資人期待的商業模式。
因此，AI需求規模有多大，與模型開發商能留下多少利潤，是兩個不同的問題。即使未來經濟活動廣泛使用AI，帶動Token需求激增，也不能直接推論最先進的模型開發商就是最大贏家。
Sparks以電力產業類比：自電力商業化以來，全球用電量大幅成長，但持有公用事業並不必然是創造巨額財富的最佳途徑。需求持續擴張，也可能伴隨高額設備支出與激烈競爭。
在他看來，將電力與運算資源轉化為Token的過程，可能更接近公用事業，而非能長期維持壟斷優勢的高利潤生意。
這項觀點並非否定AI的用途，而是提醒投資人區分技術價值與投資報酬。若模型服務日益普及、競爭壓低價格，真正獲得較大經濟效益的，可能是利用AI降低成本、改善產品與提高生產力的企業，而非投入巨資供應模型服務的業者。
paras_en: AI demand keeps expanding, but does that mean model developers can sustain high profits? Eric Peters, CIO of One River Asset Management, in an investment commentary raises another view through a conversation with investor Sparks: as financing costs rise, the AI infrastructure boom may face funding tests, and the biggest beneficiaries may not be the companies producing AI services, but the firms that effectively use those services.

In the article, Sparks is an investor and entrepreneur. He describes the current investment climate as a "typical late-stage business cycle" and argues that judging whether a market can continue requires looking beyond technology adoption rates and demand growth, also examining the flow of capital supporting investments and the cost of capital for companies.

Rising financing costs may shift the market from fear of missing out to fear of being the last buyer. Sparks says that in the later stages of a large investment cycle, financial transactions become more complex and risks harder to identify. He cites pre‑crisis collateralized debt obligations (CDOs) and re‑securitizations, noting that securities issued toward the end of a cycle tend to be more complex, harder to understand, and riskier.

In his analysis, the turning point may not start with a demand collapse but could appear first in deteriorating financing conditions. When capital costs rise, some projects that were barely viable become uneconomic, slowing overall expansion.

For bond investors, if existing bond prices fall and new issuances must offer higher yields to attract capital, risk appetite is reassessed. A more conservative supply of funds can further push up corporate financing costs, creating a reinforcing pressure loop.

"Investors shift from fearing they’ll miss out to fearing they’ll be the one left holding the bag," Sparks says. This shift won’t happen overnight, and by the time warning signs are obvious to everyone, the window for adjustment is often already missed.

He believes that a market’s major peak forms gradually, usually first pressuring financially weaker firms, which then erode the foundation supporting the broader rally. However, this is his view of market cycles and does not pinpoint the exact timing of a stock‑market turn.

AI demand does not equal high profit; model providers may resemble utilities. Beyond financing risk, the article’s core question is whether AI companies that pour massive capital into compute can build businesses with pricing power or become capital‑intensive, low‑margin competitors.

Sparks uses Amazon (AMZN‑US) as an example: stripping out AWS cloud services and advertising, its core remains retail and logistics—businesses that require heavy capital and yield limited margins. By contrast, he sees Alphabet’s (GOOGL‑US) Google, with its market position and high profitability, as closer to the business model investors desire.

Thus, the size of AI demand and the profit margin that model developers can retain are separate issues. Even if AI becomes ubiquitous in economic activity and drives a surge in token demand, it does not automatically follow that the most advanced model developers will be the biggest winners.

Sparks draws an analogy to the electricity sector: since electricity was commercialized, global consumption has surged, yet owning utilities has not necessarily been the best path to massive wealth. Expanding demand can also bring high equipment costs and fierce competition.
In his view, converting electricity and compute resources into tokens is more akin to a utility than a high‑margin, monopoly‑sustaining business.

This perspective does not deny AI’s usefulness; it reminds investors to separate technological value from investment returns. If model services become widespread and competition drives prices down, the firms that reap the biggest economic benefits are likely those that use AI to cut costs, improve products, and boost productivity—not the ones pouring huge sums into supplying model services.

items.title: 〈美股早盤〉AI股跌深有人接！晶片巨頭反攻 那指開高
items.title_en: U.S. Stocks Open Higher: AI Shares Rebound, Chip Giants Lead, Nasdaq Starts Up
paras: 美股周一(19日)開盤走高，AI相關股票在上周遭遇猛烈拋售後吸引逢低買盤，大型晶片股反彈，帶動標普500與那斯達克指數上揚，油價回落也為市場提供支撐。隨著本周重要企業財報陸續登場，投資人押注AI投資熱潮仍能支撐企業獲利，科技股成長動能能否延續將成為關注焦點。
截稿前，道瓊工業指數跌近40點或近0.07%，那斯達克綜合指數漲近270點或1.0%，標普 500 指數漲近0.6%，費城半導體指數漲近2.8%，台積電ADR漲近1.6%。
美國股指期貨周一走高，晶片股上周重挫後出現反彈，為本周財報密集公布揭開序幕。Meta(META-US)、特斯拉(TSLA-US)即將交出成績單，將再度考驗投資人對人工智慧(AI)行情的信心，焦點在於企業獲利能否支撐龐大投資，以及日益昂貴的融資成本。
那斯達克100指數期貨上漲1.3%，收復上周累跌5.5%的部分失土；標普500指數期貨上漲0.5%。一檔追蹤晶片股的ETF盤前勁揚3.6%，有望迎來10個交易日以來首度收漲。歐洲則受法國周末暴力抗議拖累，Stoxx 600指數下跌0.9%。
晶片股止跌反彈 AI融資疑慮仍未散
AI類股近期承壓，市場擔憂企業能否維持獲利高速成長，並在舉債成本攀升之際，持續支應大規模投資。
WisdomTree研究主管古普塔(Aneeka Gupta)表示，上周市場恐慌源於融資問題，而非需求轉弱，因此這波反彈有其依據，卻也同樣脆弱。
AI雲端業者CoreWeave(CRWV-US)盤前上漲逾6%，此前一周重挫25%。該公司一直處於AI企業籌資疑慮的風暴中心，旗下非投資等級債券殖利率已攀升至15%。
《彭博》策略師指出，真正風險在於融資壓力向外擴散。AI對經濟的重要性已足以讓資金緊張演變成更廣泛的成長問題，但目前證據仍有限；股市跌勢主要集中於AI融資相關標的，資金較像是在類股間輪動，而非全面撤出。
法國動盪拖累歐股 大摩看回檔醞釀機會
法國周末因生活成本問題爆發社會動盪，公共建築、商店與餐廳接連遭攻擊。但沉重債務及歐元區名列前茅的預算赤字，限制政府透過增加支出回應民怨的空間。
法國公債領跌歐洲債市，與德國公債的殖利率利差擴大，歐元也是主要貨幣中表現最弱者。美元大致持平，布蘭特原油則自五個月高點回落；美國短天期公債價格小跌，先前股市拋售曾帶動避險買盤。
花旗(C-US)歐股策略主管曼西(Beata Manthey)認為，法股波動可能延續至冬季之後，甚至下一屆總統大選，部分取決於國會能否推動債務改革。她表示，許多利空已反映在價格中，但市場仍可能反覆震盪。
摩根士丹利(MS-US)策略師威爾森(Michael Wilson)則認為，部分股市的回檔接近尾聲，優質股領先、標普500等權重指數偏弱的格局將逐漸消退。他建議投資人做好準備，無論市場快速完成調整，或跌勢緩慢延續至11月，屆時都可能是增加風險部位的機會。

威爾森指出，先前優質因子(Quality Factor)表現勝過等權重指數的偏向即將結束，這將為投資人逢低加碼股票提供絕佳機會。
威爾森在致客戶報告中明確指出：「我們建議投資人做好準備，無論是迎接快速的調整，或是延續至 11 月的緩步整理，在我們看來，屆時都將是增加風險資產而非規避風險的時機。」他強調，此輪回檔屬於買進機會而非新一波熊市的開端。
paras_en: U.S. equities opened higher on Monday (the 19th), with AI‑related stocks attracting dip‑buying after last week’s sharp sell‑off, and large‑cap chip stocks rebounding, lifting the S&P 500 and Nasdaq indexes. Lower oil prices also gave the market a boost. With a slate of major earnings reports due this week, investors are betting that the AI investment boom can still sustain corporate profits, making the continuation of tech‑stock growth momentum a key focus.

At the time of writing, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was down about 40 points, or roughly 0.07%, the Nasdaq Composite was up about 270 points, or 1.0%, the S&P 500 was up about 0.6%, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose about 2.8%, and TSMC ADR gained about 1.6%.

U.S. index futures were higher on Monday, with chip stocks bouncing back after last week’s heavy losses, setting the stage for this week’s earnings wave. Meta (META‑US) and Tesla (TSLA‑US) are about to release results, which will again test investors’ confidence in the AI rally, focusing on whether corporate earnings can support massive spending amid rising financing costs.

Nasdaq‑100 futures rose 1.3%, recapturing the 5.5% loss it had accumulated last week; S&P 500 futures were up 0.5%. An ETF that tracks chip stocks jumped 3.6% in pre‑market trading, poised for its first daily gain in ten trading days. Europe, however, was weighed down by violent protests in France over the weekend, with the Stoxx 600 slipping 0.9%.
Chip stocks stopped falling and rebounded, but AI financing concerns remain unresolved.
AI‑related shares have been under pressure lately as the market worries whether companies can keep their high profit growth while debt costs climb, yet still fund large‑scale investments.
Aneeka Gupta, research head at WisdomTree, said last week’s market panic stemmed from financing issues rather than weakening demand, so the rebound has a basis but is also fragile.

AI cloud provider CoreWeave (CRWV‑US) was up more than 6% in pre‑market trading after a 25% plunge the previous week. The company has been at the centre of the AI‑funding storm, with its non‑investment‑grade bond yields climbing to 15%.

Bloomberg strategists noted that the real risk is financing pressure spilling over. AI’s importance to the economy is enough to turn tight liquidity into a broader growth problem, though evidence is still limited; the stock‑market decline is mainly concentrated in AI‑financing‑related names, with money rotating within the sector rather than exiting entirely.
French turmoil drags down European stocks; Morgan Stanley sees pull‑back as a brewing opportunity.

France experienced social unrest over the weekend due to cost‑of‑living issues, with public buildings, shops and restaurants attacked. Heavy debt and a large budget deficit relative to the euro‑zone limit the government’s ability to respond to public anger by increasing spending.

French government bonds led the European bond market lower, widening the yield spread with German bunds, while the euro was the weakest of the major currencies. The dollar was roughly flat, Brent crude fell from a five‑month high, and short‑term U.S. Treasury prices slipped slightly after the earlier equity sell‑off sparked a flight to safety.

Beata Manthey, head of European equities strategy at Citi (C‑US), said French market volatility could persist into the winter and possibly through the next presidential election, depending in part on whether parliament can push through debt reform. She added that many downside factors are already priced in, but the market may still see repeated swings.

Michael Wilson, a strategist at Morgan Stanley (MS‑US), believes the pull‑back in some equity markets is nearing its end, and the current pattern of quality stocks leading while the S&P 500 and other heavyweight indexes lag will gradually fade. He advises investors to be ready, whether the market completes a rapid adjustment or a slower decline into November, as both scenarios could present opportunities to add risk assets.

Netflix (NFLX‑US) will report its Q3 earnings after the U.S. market close on Tuesday (the 20th). With streaming competition intensifying and user engagement showing signs of fatigue, investors are watching how the streaming giant will sustain growth. The market expects Netflix’s Q3 revenue growth to be the lowest in three years, and whether live‑streaming and advertising can provide new momentum will be the focus of the report.
Intel (INTC‑US) was up 5.56% in early trading, at $94.85 per share.

Intel (INTC‑US) rose nearly 4% in pre‑market trading after JPMorgan upgraded its rating from "Underweight" to "Neutral." Analyst Harlan Sur said that although the transformation will take several years, management’s execution has been solid, gradually boosting confidence in the company.

Amazon (AMZN‑US) rose more than 1% in pre‑market trading after Morgan Stanley named it a top‑pick and raised its target price. Analyst Brian Nowak is bullish on accelerated growth of Amazon Web Services, the potential of the Bedrock AI platform, and the use of robotics to improve operational efficiency.

Morgan Stanley chief equity strategist Michael Wilson and his team noted in a recent research note that although the S&P 500 is only about 2% below its all‑time high, valuations have already slipped significantly over the past few months, and market breadth for the benchmark index has deteriorated.
Wilson pointed out that the outperformance of the quality factor over equal‑weight indexes is waning, which could provide an excellent opportunity for investors to add stocks on dips.

In a client note, Wilson stated clearly: "We recommend investors be prepared, whether the market undergoes a rapid adjustment or a slow consolidation into November. In our view, both scenarios will be times to increase risk assets rather than avoid risk." He emphasized that this pull‑back represents a buying opportunity, not the start of a new bear market.

items.title: 不只GPU！輝達CPU搶下Modal業務 挑戰英特爾、超微
items.title_en: Not Just GPUs! Nvidia’s CPU Wins Modal Business, Challenging Intel and AMD
paras: 輝達(NVDA-US)拓展中央處理器(CPU)市場再下一城。快速成長的AI雲端新創Modal宣布，將首次採用輝達新款Vera處理器，執行可替使用者完成長時間任務的AI代理。這類工作過去全由英特爾(INTC-US)與超微(AMD-US)晶片負責，顯示輝達進軍兩大對手長期主導的市場已有初步成果。
Modal向AI開發者出租算力，上周完成由Accel領投的7.5億美元募資，估值達157.5億美元。公司表示，服務使用量已增至原本三倍，營收較去年同期成長逾15倍，未來一年營收可望達10億美元。
Modal周一(19日)表示，初步測試顯示，Vera讓AI代理可完成的工作量提高至原本兩倍，促使公司首度支援輝達的CPU設計，但也需要對軟體進行深入調整。
不過，執行長伯恩哈德森(Erik Bernhardsson)強調，Modal不會放棄既有供應商，而是將輝達晶片與英特爾、超微產品搭配使用，依各項任務需求，分配至表現最好的硬體。
他也指出，這次測試比較的是英特爾與超微已上市的晶片，兩家公司正在開發的新款產品，可能縮小與輝達的差距。Modal將在新品推出後測試，混合使用不同供應商硬體，能讓公司隨時部署效能最佳的產品。
輝達先前向投資人表示，預期本會計年度Vera銷售額至少達200億美元，藉此切入公司估計規模約2,000億美元的CPU市場。除了Modal，輝達曾透露，OpenAI、Anthropic、甲骨文(ORCL-US)及Perplexity等業者也計畫採用Vera，擴大其在AI運算領域的布局。
paras_en: Nvidia (NVDA-US) scores another win as it expands into the central processing unit (CPU) market. Fast‑growing AI cloud startup Modal announced it will for the first time use Nvidia’s new Vera processor to run AI agents that can handle long‑duration tasks for users. Such workloads have historically been handled exclusively by Intel (INTC-US) and AMD (AMD-US) chips, showing that Nvidia is beginning to make inroads into a market long dominated by its two biggest rivals.

Modal rents compute power to AI developers and last week closed a $750 million financing round led by Accel, valuing the company at $15.75 billion. The firm said usage of its services has risen to three times its prior level and revenue has grown more than 15‑fold year‑over‑year, with revenue expected to reach $1 billion within the next year.

On Monday (the 19th), Modal reported that early tests show Vera doubles the amount of work AI agents can accomplish, prompting the company to support Nvidia’s CPU design for the first time, though it also requires deep software adjustments.

However, CEO Erik Bernhardsson stressed that Modal will not abandon its existing suppliers; instead it will pair Nvidia chips with Intel and AMD products, allocating tasks to the hardware that delivers the best performance for each workload.

He also noted that the comparison in this test involved Intel’s and AMD’s currently available chips, and that new products the two companies are developing could narrow the gap with Nvidia. Modal will test after the new releases, and a hybrid approach using hardware from different vendors will allow the company to deploy the most efficient solutions at any time.

Nvidia previously told investors it expects Vera sales to reach at least $20 billion this fiscal year, giving it a foothold in the roughly $200 billion CPU market it estimates. In addition to Modal, Nvidia has disclosed that OpenAI, Anthropic, Oracle (ORCL-US) and Perplexity also plan to use Vera, expanding its footprint in AI computing.

items.title: 美股兩大力量死鬥！美債殖利率狂飆 AI股賺翻也難漲
items.title_en: U.S. Stocks Clash Between Two Forces: Soaring Treasury Yields and AI Stocks Struggle to Rise
paras: 華爾街正迎來一場高風險的正面交鋒。科技與能源巨頭亮眼的企業獲利，正硬生生撞上持續狂飆的債券殖利率。
在人工智慧（AI）技術基礎設施與資料中心建置潮的推動下，法人分析師預期企業獲利將持續強勁成長。正是這份高昂的期待，支撐著標普500等主要指數今年一路克服多重利空。
伊朗局勢推升國際油價衝破每桶百元大關，讓本就承受高物價壓力的消費者負擔加劇；與此同時，10年期與30年期美國公債殖利率攀升至數十年新高，更為股市增添了一道沉重的逆風。
市場走向雙軌化：AI概念股獨撐大局後轉弱
殖利率飆升加劇了美股市場的分化。阿波羅全球管理公司首席經濟學家史洛克（Torsten Slok）指出，當前市場已裂變為「AI概念股」與「非AI概念股」兩大陣營。
自8月起，大盤漲勢明顯收窄，即使大多數個股陷入苦戰，主要指數表面上仍維持高檔。這股平衡直到過去一週才破功，原先強勢的AI概念股突然遭遇賣壓。
雪上加霜的是，即使油價持續走高，美債殖利率出現回檔，反映市場避險情緒升溫；投資人則順勢轉回先前受高利率壓抑的類股與個股。
財報門檻大幅提高：投資人開始質疑AI成長故事
數月以來，投資人將焦點全數鎖定在獲利表現，使AI概念股幾乎免疫於小型股及其他利率敏感股所承受的打擊。
然而，隨著市場對AI驅動的成長敘事開始存疑，這些股票要繼續推升股價的門檻已大幅提高。
在大型銀行與百事可樂（PepsiCo）等消費巨頭搶先公布的財報未能驚艷市場後，恢復市場信心 重擔，已落在即將公布最新財測與業績的AI核心受益股身上。
Nationwide首席市場策略師哈克特（Mark Hackett）直言：「市場的疑慮正持續升溫。」
獲利爆發力對決資金成本：估值修正引發長短力道拉鋸
隨著債券殖利率上周五(16日)繼續攀升，市場似乎正走向兩股強大力量的拉鋸。
Founders 100 ETF投資組合經理莫納漢（Michael Monaghan）表示，一方面，企業獲利成長速度已達到通常只有經濟復甦初期才會出現的強勁水準；另一方面，推升債券殖利率的力量，短期內似乎不太可能消退。
莫納漢表示：「市場正處於拉鋸之中。儘管今年以來股市上漲，但相較於明年的獲利預估，目前股價已便宜許多。」
雖然股價仍有支撐，估值，也就是投資人願意為每一美元預期獲利支付的價格，卻已明顯下滑。根據FactSet資料，截至上周五，標普500指數的預估本益比為19倍，低於過去5年與10年的平均水準。
富達投資全球總經主管提默（Jurrien Timmer）表示，認為科技股能免受日益加劇的總體經濟壓力影響，並不完全正確。
提默在訪談中表示：「可以把它想成獲利成長在分子、資金成本在分母。目前獲利正突飛猛進，但資金成本也在上升。兩者正在競速，就看哪一方對股價的影響更大。」
paras_en: Wall Street is facing a high‑risk head‑to‑head battle. Stellar earnings from tech and energy giants are colliding head‑on with continuously soaring bond yields.

Driven by the wave of AI infrastructure and data‑center construction, sell‑side analysts expect corporate earnings to keep growing strongly. This lofty expectation has helped major indices such as the S&P 500 overcome multiple headwinds this year.

Iran’s situation has pushed international oil prices above $100 a barrel, further burdening consumers already feeling high price pressure; at the same time, 10‑year and 30‑year U.S. Treasury yields have climbed to multi‑decade highs, adding a heavy headwind for equities.
The market is moving on two tracks: AI‑related stocks, after initially supporting the market, are now weakening.

Yield spikes have intensified the split in the U.S. equity market. Torsten Slok, chief economist at Apollo Global Management, notes that the market has now fractured into two camps – “AI‑themed stocks” and “non‑AI stocks.”

Since August, the broad market’s rally has noticeably narrowed. Even though many individual stocks are struggling, the main indices have superficially stayed at elevated levels. This balance only broke in the past week, when once‑strong AI stocks suddenly faced selling pressure.

Adding insult to injury, even as oil prices keep rising, Treasury yields have pulled back, reflecting heightened market‑risk aversion; investors are shifting back into sectors and stocks that were previously suppressed by high rates.
Earnings thresholds have risen sharply: investors begin to doubt the AI growth story
For months, investors have focused exclusively on earnings performance, making AI‑themed stocks almost immune to the blows that hit small‑caps and other rate‑sensitive stocks.
However, as the market’s confidence in AI‑driven growth narratives wanes, the hurdle for these stocks to keep pushing prices higher has risen dramatically.

After earnings from large banks and consumer giants such as PepsiCo failed to wow the market, the burden of restoring confidence now falls on AI‑core beneficiaries that are about to release fresh forecasts and results.
Mark Hackett, chief market strategist at Nationwide, said plainly: “Market concerns are continuing to heat up.”
Earnings explosiveness versus funding costs: valuation adjustments spark a tug‑of‑war between long and short forces
With bond yields continuing to climb on Friday the 16th, the market appears to be caught in a tug‑of‑war between two powerful forces.

Michael Monaghan, portfolio manager of the Founders 100 ETF, said that on one hand, corporate earnings growth has reached a robust pace normally seen only in the early stages of an economic recovery; on the other hand, the forces driving yields higher seem unlikely to subside in the short term.
Monaghan added: “The market is in a tug‑of‑war. Although stocks have risen so far this year, relative to next year’s earnings outlook, today’s prices are already much cheaper.”

While stock prices still have support, valuations – the price investors are willing to pay for each dollar of expected earnings – have clearly slipped. According to FactSet, as of last Friday the S&P 500’s forward P/E ratio stood at 19×, below the five‑year and ten‑year averages.
Jurrien Timmer, global chief economist at Fidelity Investments, said it is not entirely correct to think technology stocks are insulated from the growing macro‑economic pressures.

Timmer explained in an interview: “You can think of it as earnings growth in the numerator and funding costs in the denominator. Earnings are surging, but funding costs are rising too. The two are racing, and it will depend on which side has the bigger impact on stock prices.”

items.title_en: Factory Automation Hits 80%: Siemens Teams Up with Nvidia to Boost Manufacturing Competitiveness with AI
paras: 西門子(SIEGY-US)執行董事奈克(Cedrik Neike)周一(19日)表示，公司計畫運用人工智慧(AI)，將工廠製造流程的自動化程度由目前的30%至40%，提高至70%至80%，藉此提升生產效率，協助德國等高薪資國家留住製造業工作機會。
奈克在西門子位於德國埃爾朗根(Erlangen)的電子工廠表示，製造商必須每年實現7%至9%的生產力成長，才能維持競爭力。他認為，AI帶動的自動化升級，有助於高薪資國家維持製造業競爭優勢。
西門子正與輝達(NVDA-US)合作，推動「實體AI」在製造業的應用，透過數位孿生與AI模型，先在虛擬環境中模擬、優化工廠運作，再將成果導入實際生產現場。
西門子也計畫將埃爾朗根電子工廠打造成AI製造示範基地，並於2030年前投入5億歐元，約合5.61億美元，擴建廠區。
paras_en: Siemens (SIEGY-US) Executive Director Cedrik Neike said on Monday (the 19th) that the company plans to use artificial intelligence (AI) to raise the automation level of factory manufacturing processes from the current 30‑40% to 70‑80%, thereby improving production efficiency and helping high‑wage countries such as Germany retain manufacturing jobs.

Neike explained at Siemens' electronics plant in Erlangen, Germany, that manufacturers must achieve 7%‑9% productivity growth each year to stay competitive. He believes that AI‑driven automation upgrades will help high‑wage nations maintain a manufacturing advantage.

Siemens is collaborating with Nvidia (NVDA-US) to promote the use of “physical AI” in manufacturing, employing digital twins and AI models to simulate and optimise plant operations in a virtual environment before applying the results to real‑world production lines.
Siemens also intends to turn the Erlangen electronics plant into an AI‑manufacturing demonstration hub, investing €500 million (about $561 million) by 2030 to expand the facility.

paras: 台北金融市場今(19) 日「股匯雙殺」再現，受到美股震盪及國際避險情緒升溫影響，外資持續大舉撤資，三大法人合計賣超台股899.54億元，加權指數一度重挫941點，台積電 (2330-TW) (TSM-US) 等權值股尾盤急拉，終場下跌289.18點，收在46822.08點。匯市在資金大量淨匯出壓力下，新台幣兌美元匯率開低走低，盤中一度觸及32.572元低點，終場重貶1.07角收在32.445元，兩大外匯市場爆出38.53億美元的大量。
觀察台股法人動態，三大法人今日資金操作分歧明顯。外資及陸資延續偏空態度，單日賣超高達767.43億元，寫下連續9個交易日賣超紀錄；自營商也站在賣方，賣超362.63億元；僅投信法人獨撐大局，逆勢買超230.51億元，展現強烈護盤意願。

paras_en: Taipei's financial markets saw a repeat of the "stock‑currency double kill" today (19th) as US equity volatility and rising global risk‑off sentiment prompted foreign investors to pull out large amounts of capital. The three major institutional investors collectively sold a net 89.954 billion TWD of Taiwanese equities, and the weighted index plunged as much as 941 points before ending down 289.18 points at 46,822.08. Meanwhile, under heavy net outflows in the foreign exchange market, the New Taiwan dollar weakened against the US dollar, briefly hitting a low of 32.572 TWD per USD before closing down 0.107 to 32.445, with the two major FX markets reporting a combined outflow of $3.853 billion.

Looking at the activity of Taiwan's institutional investors, today's fund flows showed a clear divergence. Foreign and mainland Chinese investors maintained a bearish stance, net selling a record 76.743 billion TWD in a single day, marking the ninth consecutive trading day of net outflows. Proprietary traders also sold, netting 36.263 billion TWD. Only investment trusts stood on the buying side, net purchasing 23.051 billion TWD, demonstrating a strong willingness to support the market.

The market's capital structure continued to adjust today, causing the index to tumble sharply at the open and dip to a intraday low of 46,170 points, testing the seasonal (quarterly) support line. Fortunately, semiconductor stocks such as TSMC rallied in the closing minutes, pulling the index back toward the flat line and narrowing the overall decline.

In the FX market, the TWD opened at 32.36 per USD but was quickly pressured lower by strong foreign outflows, falling to a low of 32.572 during the session. Facing a rapid, large‑scale withdrawal of foreign capital, the central bank issued a rare emergency statement mid‑session to steady confidence and intervened by selling dollars to provide liquidity. The Taipei foreign‑exchange market closed the TWD at 32.445, a depreciation of 0.107, with transaction volume expanding to $2.831 billion.

The Yuan‑Tai foreign‑exchange market closed the TWD at 32.468, a depreciation of 0.12, with a transaction volume of $1.022 billion. Combined, the two major FX markets saw total turnover rise to $3.853 billion, indicating extremely active trading and fierce battles between buyers and sellers.

items.title: 印尼股票市場拋售加劇 並蔓延至債券與印尼盾
items.title_en: Indonesia Stock Market Sell‑Off Intensifies and Spreads to Bonds and Rupiah
paras: 印尼雅加達綜合指數(JCI)持續下挫，周一(19日)盤中一度重挫5.4%，延續上周五崩跌12%的頹勢。此次下跌，主要受到指數編算公司摩根士丹利資本國際(MSCI Inc.)發出潛在降級警告影響。
相關衝擊造成印尼金融市場拋售潮全面擴大，股市陷入近30年來最嚴重暴跌，賣壓並迅速延燒至債券與印尼盾匯市。
MSCI 上周五表示，出於可投資性等疑慮，正考慮將印尼從「新興市場」直接降級至「獨立市場」，此舉遠超今年1月警示降至「邊境市場」的幅度。措手不及的印尼官方已安排於周一與 MSCI 高層會面尋求釐清。
高盛估算，若印尼被完全剔除，可能觸發約56億美元的被動型資金撤出，若富時羅素(FTSE Russell)跟進，恐再面臨27億美元流出風險。2026年截至目前，外資已從印尼股市淨撤出51億美元，創下歷史最大年度外流紀錄。
針對市場崩盤與資金外逃，新加坡東斯銀行(SEB)亞洲策略主管 Eugenia Victorino 指出：「外資正全線撤離印尼股市，債市也感受到熱度。印尼盾走弱正侵蝕實質殖利率，在匯率止穩前，全球資金寧可安全地位於場外觀望。」
PT MNC Sekuritas 分析師 Herditya Wicaksana 表示：「賣壓依然顯著，特別是像大型銀行這類對雅加達綜合指數影響巨大的股票。」
星展集團(DBS Group) 警告，衝擊可能進一步蔓延並緊縮融資條件，推升10年期國債殖利率邁向7.5%，並促使印尼央行再升息50至100個基點。
為遏止跌勢，印尼證券交易所周一緊急調緊單一股票每日最大跌幅限制，由15%縮減至7%，施行至今年底
。企業端也展開自救，富豪 Prajogo Pangestu 旗下三家公司計畫合計買回2.5兆印尼盾(約1.38億美元)庫藏股；金光集團旗下 PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa 也提議買回1兆印尼盾股票。
paras_en: Indonesia’s Jakarta Composite Index (JCI) kept sliding, plunging as much as 5.4% during Monday’s (the 19th) session, extending the 12% crash that began last Friday. The drop was mainly triggered by a potential downgrade warning issued by the index‑calculating firm MSCI Inc.

The fallout sparked a broad sell‑off across Indonesia’s financial markets, with the equity market experiencing its steepest plunge in nearly 30 years and selling pressure quickly spilling over into bonds and the rupiah foreign‑exchange market.

MSCI said on Friday that, due to concerns over investability, it is considering moving Indonesia from the “Emerging Markets” category directly to “Standalone Market,” a step far beyond the warning in January that it might be demoted to a “Frontier Market.” Caught off guard, Indonesian officials have arranged a meeting with senior MSCI officials on Monday to seek clarification.

Goldman Sachs estimates that a full removal of Indonesia could trigger about $5.6 billion of passive‑fund outflows, and if FTSE Russell follows suit, another $2.7 billion could flee. To date in 2026, foreign investors have net‑withdrawn $5.1 billion from Indonesia’s stock market, setting a record for the largest annual outflow.

Commenting on the market crash and capital flight, Eugenia Victorino, head of Asian strategy at Singapore’s SEB, said: “Foreign investors are pulling out of Indonesian equities across the board, and the bond market is feeling the heat. A weaker rupiah is eroding real yields, and until the currency stabilises, global capital would rather stay safely off‑exchange and wait.”
Herditya Wicaksana, an analyst at PT MNC Sekuritas, noted: “Selling pressure remains significant, especially in stocks like large banks that have a huge impact on the Jakarta Composite Index.”

DBS Group warned that the shock could spread further and tighten financing conditions, pushing the 10‑year government bond yield toward 7.5% and prompting the Bank of Indonesia to raise rates by another 50 to 100 basis points.

To curb the decline, the Indonesia Stock Exchange on Monday urgently tightened the daily maximum price‑move limit for individual stocks, cutting it from 15% to 7% effective through the end of the year.

Companies are also taking self‑help measures: billionaire Prajogo Pangestu’s three firms plan to repurchase a total of 2.5 trillion rupiah (about $138 million) of shares, and PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa of the Golden Light Group has proposed buying back 1 trillion rupiah of stock.

items.title: 人工智慧浪潮助推 馬來西亞9月出口額創逾5年新高
items.title_en: AI Wave Boosts Malaysia's September Export Value to Over Five-Year High
paras: 受惠於全球人工智慧(AI)浪潮與資料中心建置帶動的半導體及電子產品需求，馬來西亞今年9月外貿展現強勁成長力道，出口額刷新逾5年來最高紀錄。
根據馬來西亞統計局(DOSM)與投資貿易暨工業部(MITI)公布的最新數據，馬來西亞9月出口額達2,151億令吉(約合450億美元)，年增54.5%，表現遠超出《路透》調查預期的44.6%及《彭博》預估的39.9%。
在進出口同步雙位數成長帶動下，9月總貿易額年增53.7%至3,965億令吉。進口額則年增52.7%至1,814億令吉，高於市場預期的39%，9月貿易順差擴大約65%至337億令吉，高於預期的316億令吉。
統計局資料顯示，進口擴張主要由生產輸入端需求強勁所推升，其中中間財進口大增69.6%至921億令吉，資本財與消費財進口亦分別成長20.9%及18.2%。
從主要出口商品來看，占總出口半數以上的電子與電器產品(E&E)9月出口額年增率高達68%至69.2%，創下單月歷史新高。包含半導體測試儀器在內的光學與科學設備出口額亦同步登頂。
出口市場方面，對台灣出口年增率高達175.2%(成長超過一倍)，對美國出口成長89.9%，對中國出口則成長22.1%。相對地，受棕櫚油出口減少拖累，農業出口年減5.7%。
針對未來外貿展望，馬來西亞投資貿工部在官方聲明中特別警示：「馬來西亞的貿易表現仍面臨主要經濟體貿易政策轉變及地緣政治緊張局勢帶來的不確定性。」
MITI 分析，尤其是中東地區持續的衝突可能打亂全球貿易流動並加劇成本壓力。MITI 表示未來將持續「評估相關發展、加強市場多元化、擴大進入高成長市場，並協助馬來西亞出口商進行調整」，以增強外貿抗風險能力。
paras_en: Benefiting from the global artificial intelligence (AI) wave and the demand for semiconductors and electronic products driven by data‑center construction, Malaysia’s foreign trade showed strong growth in September, with export value reaching a record high not seen in more than five years.

According to the latest data released by Malaysia’s Department of Statistics (DOSM) and the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI), September export value hit RM215.1 billion (about US$45 billion), up 54.5% year‑on‑year, far exceeding Reuters’ forecast of 44.6% and Bloomberg’s estimate of 39.9%.

With both imports and exports posting double‑digit growth, total trade in September rose 53.7% year‑on‑year to RM396.5 billion. Imports increased 52.7% to RM181.4 billion, above the market’s 39% expectation, and the trade surplus widened about 65% to RM33.7 billion, higher than the anticipated RM31.6 billion.

Statistics show that the import expansion was mainly driven by strong demand for production inputs, with intermediate goods imports surging 69.6% to RM92.1 billion, while capital goods and consumer goods imports grew 20.9% and 18.2% respectively.

Looking at major export commodities, electronic and electrical (E&E) products, which account for more than half of total exports, posted a year‑on‑year growth of 68% to RM69.2 billion, setting a new monthly historical high. Exports of optical and scientific equipment, including semiconductor testing instruments, also hit record levels.

In terms of export markets, shipments to Taiwan jumped 175.2% year‑on‑year (more than double), to the United States grew 89.9%, and to China rose 22.1%. Conversely, agricultural exports fell 5.7% year‑on‑year due to a drop in palm‑oil shipments.

Regarding the outlook, MITI warned in an official statement that “Malaysia’s trade performance still faces uncertainty from major economies’ shifting trade policies and heightened geopolitical tensions.”

MITI analysis notes that ongoing conflicts in the Middle East could disrupt global trade flows and increase cost pressures. It said Malaysia will continue to “assess developments, strengthen market diversification, expand entry into high‑growth markets, and help exporters adjust,” to boost the resilience of its foreign trade.

items.title_en: Far East Commercial Bank: US Rate‑Hike Expectations Cool, Dollar Generally Weakens
paras: ◆USD/JPY

美國聯邦準備理事會(FED)主席沃什雖對美國經濟韌性表示樂觀，且稱受益人工智能推動，並向其他領域擴展的投資熱潮，正引發短期需求衝擊，從而對通脹形成上行壓力，但拒絕透露關於今年剩餘時間的會議上可能採取的行動，使得美元承壓；此外，日本央行(BOJ)總裁植田和男表示，確保基礎通脹率穩定在BOJ 2%的通脹目標附近正變得越來越重要，且據路透公布一項調查顯示，隨著中東衝突推動能源價格上漲的影響正逐步傳導至家庭，日本9月核心消費者通脹率可能自12月以來首次超過BOJ 2%的目標，另外美國財政部次長Erin Browne指出，日本已不再面臨持續十餘年的通縮環境，其匯率水平與貨幣政策必須相應調整，並隨著日本投資人截至10月10日當週連續第四週淨賣出外國債券，延續了撤離海外債市的趨勢，提供日圓支撐，令美元兌日圓下降至157.67低點。

隨後據美國官方公布9月數據顯示，工業生產及製造業產出分別成長0.7%及0.3%，且衡量企業資源利用程度的產能利用率升至76.9%，另外進口及出口物價月率漲幅分別為1.1%及2.2%，皆超過市場預期，且進口物價同比上漲8.1%，漲幅為2022年7月以來最大，這進一步表明，隨著中東衝突持續，美國國內通脹壓力正在加劇，推動美元兌日圓走升至158.33高點。預估今日美元兌日圓阻力於158.10-30，支撐於157.30-50。
◆EUR/USD

澳洲疲軟的就業數據表現，促使投資人下調對澳洲央行(RBA)今年第五次加息的押注，拖累澳幣走勢，但相較於紐西蘭央行(RBNZ)首席經濟學家康韋在接受彭博新聞採訪時稱下一次利率調整一切皆有可能，隨著調期市場數據顯示，RBNZ在10月28日將利率上調25個基點概率為86%，為紐元提供支撐，而且國際貨幣基金(IMF)預計歐洲央行(ECB)於2026年至少加息25個基點，提振歐元兌美元觸及1.1269高點。
據歐盟統計局公布歐元區9月消費者物價調和指數(HICP)月率及年率分別上升0.6%及3.8%，符合預期，但8月未經季節性調整貿易數據意外錄得逆差161億歐元，且據IMF指出法國借貸成本短期內仍屬可控，但財政整頓壓力恐將加大，打擊歐元兌美元至1.1206低點。預估今日歐元兌美元支撐於1.1190-1.1210，阻力於1.1260-80。
◆GBP/USD

週五英國央行(BOE)總裁貝利於出席國際金融協會(IIF)時表示英國通脹率高於目標水平，但迄今為止，能源價格飆升似乎對英國物價廣泛影響有限，令英鎊兌美元盤整於1.3263低點；隨後美國FED主席沃什未對美國強勁的CPI及PPI數據置評，使得10月FED加息的概率也因沃什的言論而下降，相較於路透調查的多數經濟學家預測，BOE將於11月將指標利率上調至4.0%，這將是該行三年多來的首次加息，激勵英鎊兌美元漲至三週高點1.3371。預估今日英鎊兌美元支撐於1.3290-1.3310，阻力於1.3370-90。

Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell expressed optimism about the resilience of the U.S. economy and said that the investment boom spurred by artificial‑intelligence advances and its spill‑over into other sectors is creating short‑term demand pressure that could push inflation higher. He declined to reveal what actions might be taken at the remaining meetings this year, leaving the dollar under pressure. Meanwhile, Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said it is becoming increasingly important to keep core‑inflation near the BOJ’s 2% target, and a Reuters poll shows that rising energy prices from the Middle‑East conflict are gradually passing through to households. Japan’s core CPI for September could exceed the BOJ’s 2% goal for the first time since December. U.S. Treasury Deputy Secretary Erin Browne added that Japan is no longer in a decade‑long deflationary environment, so its exchange‑rate level and monetary policy must adjust. Japanese investors have sold foreign bonds for the fourth consecutive week as of the week ending Oct. 10, continuing the pull‑out from overseas bond markets, which supports the yen and pushed USD/JPY down to a low of 157.67.

Subsequent U.S. official data for September showed industrial production up 0.7% and manufacturing output up 0.3%, while capacity utilization rose to 76.9%. Import and export prices rose 1.1% and 2.2% month‑over‑month, both above expectations, and import prices jumped 8.1% year‑over‑year – the biggest rise since July 2022. The figures indicate that, as the Middle‑East conflict persists, domestic inflation pressure in the United States is intensifying, driving the dollar up to a high of 158.33 against the yen. The market expects resistance for USD/JPY around 158.10‑30 and support around 157.30‑50.
EUR/USD

The International Monetary Fund also projects that the European Central Bank will lift rates by at least 25 basis points in 2026, helping the euro climb to a high of 1.1269 against the dollar.

However, seasonally‑adjusted trade data for August unexpectedly posted a €16.1 billion deficit. The IMF noted that France’s short‑term borrowing costs remain manageable, but fiscal‑adjustment pressure could increase, pushing EUR/USD down to a low of 1.1206. The market expects support for the euro around 1.1190‑1.1210 and resistance around 1.1260‑1.1280.
GBP/USD

Later, Fed Chair Jerome Powell did not comment on the strong U.S. CPI and PPI numbers, reducing the perceived probability of an October Fed hike. items.title: 台幣逼近32.5元還會貶？外銀看好強勁出口支撐 年底反攻31.5元
items.title_en: Taiwan Dollar Near 32.5 per Dollar – Will It Depreciate Further? Foreign Banks See Strong Export Support, Expect a Rebound to 31.5 by Year‑End
paras: 分析師表示，全球市場對人工智慧（AI）交易的疑慮引發新台幣走弱，卻掩蓋了台灣經濟的基本韌性；穩健的經濟基本面可望支撐新台幣在年底前回升。
儘管新台幣近期承受沉重壓力，華僑銀行與荷蘭國際集團（ING）仍預期，新台幣將分別回升至兌1美元31.60元與31.50元，較目前水準升值約2%。
這些預測的依據，是台灣強勁的經濟成長與經常帳順差。儘管市場對AI股高估值的疑慮持續推動資金外流，短期壓抑匯率，分析師預期，未來幾個月貿易基本面的支撐終將占上風。
三菱日聯銀行（MUFG）亞洲全球市場研究主管Lin Li表示：「創紀錄的貿易順差與AI相關出口，持續為新台幣提供基本支撐。但外資證券投資流出、對外投資，以及美元與新台幣之間龐大的利差，目前正創造美元需求，抵銷這些支撐。」
她預期，新台幣年底前將升至兌1美元31.8元，並在2027年6月底進一步升至30.9元。
出口與順差強勁 外資撤出台股形成拉鋸
受全球先進晶片需求空前強勁帶動，台灣經常帳順差在2025年底達到近700億美元的歷史新高，近幾個月則溫和收窄。同時，政府將全年經濟成長率預測上修至逾10%，台灣可望迎來2010年以來首次雙位數成長。
不過，這些基本面優勢正與外資撤離潮相互拉鋸。外資周四賣超台股新台幣3,026億元（約93億美元），創單日新高，推動新台幣逼近今年以來兌1美元約32.50元的低點。
雖然分析師不認為這個價位是央行必須捍衛的防線，但仍密切關注，視其為央行可接受匯率區間的重要參考。
ING大中華區首席經濟學家宋林表示：「央行將試圖讓新台幣維持相對區間震盪。我不認為存在必須守住的明確防線，但今年以來，31.5至32.5元似乎一直是央行可以接受的區間。」
道富銀行亞太區總體策略師Jiuk Choi認為，央行更可能著重降低匯率波動，而非鎖定特定價位。他表示：「話雖如此，我們認為美元兌新台幣32.4至32.5元是重要區間，因為這是2026年以來的高點。」
油價與利差添壓力 中期仍看升
除了科技業疑慮，台灣作為能源進口國，偏高的原油價格也為新台幣增添壓力。此外，美國10年期公債殖利率較台灣同天期公債高出約300個基點，具吸引力的利差持續支撐美元普遍走強，壓抑區域貨幣表現。
LGT私人銀行外匯與利率專家Trang Le表示：「短期逆風包括外資撤出台股，以及聯準會立場偏鷹帶動美元走強。」
她指出：「即便如此，強勁的出口動能、穩健的對外收支，以及AI驅動的半導體景氣循環，仍使新台幣中期走勢偏向升值。我們預期，匯率波動將是主軸，而非持續走弱。」
科技財報成下一個匯率關鍵
匯市交易員正關注主要半導體製造商的財報，策略師視其為牽動跨境股市資金流向與匯率波動的下一個關鍵因素。台積電周四公布優於預期的營收展望，卻未能完全平息市場對整體AI基礎建設擴張的疑慮。
道富銀行的Choi表示：「接下來公布的全球科技業財報，可能加劇新台幣波動，尤其市場對AI相關資本支出、獲利能力及中國競爭的敏感度已升高。」
他認為，AI交易疑慮仍可能讓新台幣短期進一步走弱，但預期年底前將回升至兌1美元31.80元。
他表示：「我們認為，新台幣是對沖美元走強的最佳貨幣之一，因為資本與經常帳資金流仍然強勁，而且新台幣也是新興市場中波動率最低的貨幣之一。」
paras_en: Analysts say that global concerns over artificial‑intelligence (AI) trading have weakened the New Taiwan dollar, but this masks the underlying resilience of Taiwan’s economy; a solid economic foundation is expected to support a rebound of the currency before year‑end.

Even though the New Taiwan dollar has been under heavy pressure recently, both OCBC and ING forecast that it will recover to about NT$31.60 per US$1 and NT$31.50 per US$1 respectively, roughly a 2% appreciation from current levels.

These forecasts are based on Taiwan’s strong economic growth and current‑account surplus. Although market worries about over‑valued AI stocks continue to drive capital outflows and suppress the exchange rate in the short term, analysts expect the trade fundamentals to ultimately prevail in the coming months.

Lin Li, head of Asian Global Markets Research at MUFG, said: “Record‑high trade surpluses and AI‑related exports continuously provide fundamental support for the New Taiwan dollar. Yet foreign‑security outflows, outbound investment and the huge interest‑rate differential between the dollar and the New Taiwan dollar are currently creating dollar demand that offsets those supports.”
She projects the New Taiwan dollar will rise to NT$31.8 per US$1 by year‑end and further to NT$30.9 by the end of June 2027.
Strong exports and surplus, foreign‑capital pull‑out creates a tug‑of‑war in Taiwan equities

Fueled by unprecedented demand for advanced chips worldwide, Taiwan’s current‑account surplus is set to hit a historic high of nearly US$70 billion by the end of 2025, though it has narrowed modestly in recent months. At the same time, the government has lifted its full‑year growth forecast to above 10%, positioning Taiwan for its first double‑digit expansion since 2010.

However, these fundamental strengths are being contested by a wave of foreign‑capital outflows. On Thursday foreign investors sold NT$3,026 billion (about US$9.3 billion) of Taiwan equities, a single‑day record, pushing the New Taiwan dollar toward this year’s low of roughly NT$32.50 per US$1.
While analysts do not view this level as a hard floor the central bank must defend, they are watching it closely as an important reference for the exchange‑rate band the bank may tolerate.

Song Lin, chief economist for Greater China at ING, said: “The central bank will try to keep the New Taiwan dollar within a relative range. I don’t see a clear floor that must be defended, but since the start of the year the NT$31.5‑NT$32.5 band has seemed acceptable to the central bank.”

Jiuk Choi, global‑strategy head for Asia‑Pacific at State Street, believes the central bank is more likely to focus on reducing volatility rather than anchoring a specific level. He added: “That said, we see NT$32.4‑NT$32.5 per US$1 as a key zone because it marks the high point reached in 2026.”
Oil prices and interest‑rate spreads add pressure; medium‑term outlook still upward

Beyond tech‑sector concerns, Taiwan’s status as an energy‑importing nation means high crude‑oil prices add further pressure on the New Taiwan dollar. In addition, the U.S. 10‑year Treasury yield is about 300 basis points higher than Taiwan’s comparable bond, and the attractive spread continues to underpin a broadly strong dollar, suppressing regional currencies.
Trang Le, FX and rates specialist at LGT Private Bank, said: “Short‑term headwinds include foreign‑capital outflows from Taiwan equities and a hawkish Fed stance that is bolstering the dollar.”

She noted: “Even so, strong export momentum, solid external balances and an AI‑driven semiconductor cycle still tilt the medium‑term New Taiwan dollar trend toward appreciation. We expect exchange‑rate volatility to be the main driver, not a continued weakening.”
Tech earnings become the next exchange‑rate catalyst

FX traders are watching earnings reports from major semiconductor manufacturers, which strategists see as the next key factor influencing cross‑border equity flows and currency moves. TSMC’s Thursday earnings outlook beat expectations, but did not fully allay market concerns about the broader AI‑infrastructure expansion.

State Street’s Choi said: “The upcoming global tech earnings season could amplify New Taiwan dollar volatility, especially as market sensitivity to AI‑related capex, profitability and competition from China has risen.”
He believes AI‑trading worries could still push the New Taiwan dollar lower in the short term, but expects a rebound to NT$31.80 per US$1 by year‑end.

He added: “We see the New Taiwan dollar as one of the best hedges against a strong dollar because capital and current‑account flows remain robust, and the New Taiwan dollar is also among the least volatile currencies in emerging markets.”

items.title: 美烏矛盾與法國騷亂推升美元！歐元兌多數G10貨幣走貶 今早兌美元一度大跌0.5%
items.title_en: US-Ukraine Tensions and French Unrest Boost the Dollar! Euro Falls Against Most G10 Currencies, Briefly Dropping 0.5% Against the Dollar This Morning
paras: 受美烏矛盾進一步升高及法國大規模抗議活動影響，市場對歐元信心受挫，歐元兌多數G10貨幣在今(19)日亞洲早盤交易時段走低。
周末期間，法國多個城市抗議活動演變為警方與示威者之間的衝突，爆發法國多年來最嚴重的街頭暴力事件，出現搶劫、地標建築遭縱火情況。歐洲多國接連發生示威活動，法國的抗議規模最大，比利時、義大利、葡萄牙也受到波及。與此同時，烏克蘭總統澤倫斯基周日(18日)指責川普試圖向基輔施壓，逼迫烏克蘭向俄羅斯投降。
歐元兌美元在今日早盤一度貶值0.5%，最低貶至 1.1183 美元，隨後部分收復跌幅，交投於 1.1212 美元附近。受歐元走弱拖累，東歐貨幣表現弱於其他新興市場貨幣，美元兌波蘭茲羅提升值0.5%，報3.9071；美元兌匈牙利福林走升0.5%，報324.88，美元兌保加利亞列弗亦升值0.5%，報1.7485。
澳洲聯邦銀行外匯策略師Carol Kong表示：「市場恐將持續為歐元計入風險溢價。歐元兌美元本周可能測試 1.1130支撐價位，尤其是在地緣緊張進一步推高美元的情況下。」
paras_en: Rising US‑Ukraine tensions and large‑scale protests in France have dented market confidence in the euro, causing the euro to fall against most G10 currencies during Asian early‑trade on the 19th.

Over the weekend, protests in several French cities escalated into clashes between police and demonstrators, sparking the most severe street violence France has seen in years, including robberies and arson of landmark buildings. Demonstrations spread across multiple European countries, with France seeing the largest protests, and Belgium, Italy and Portugal also affected. At the same time, Ukrainian President Zelensky on Sunday (the 18th) accused former U.S. President Trump of trying to pressure Kyiv into surrendering to Russia.

The euro‑dollar pair slipped as much as 0.5% in early trade today, hitting a low of 1.1183 USD before partially regaining ground and trading around 1.1212 USD. The euro’s weakness also weighed on Eastern European currencies, which underperformed other emerging‑market currencies: the dollar rose 0.5% against the Polish zloty to 3.9071, against the Hungarian forint to 324.88, and against the Bulgarian lev to 1.7485.

Carol Kong, FX strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, said: “The market is likely to continue pricing a risk premium into the euro. The euro‑dollar pair could test the 1.1130 support level this week, especially if geopolitical tensions further lift the dollar.”

items.title: 阿拉伯半島周遭海域周末頻傳商船遇襲！伊朗警告：美若恢復攻擊  已有「新作戰計畫」
items.title_en: Commercial Ships Frequently Attacked Around the Arabian Peninsula Over the Weekend; Iran Warns of a New Operational Plan if the U.S. Resumes Attacks
paras: 伊朗最高國家安全委員會秘書雷札伊周日(18日)警告，已針對美國與以色列「任何新的冒險行徑」擬定回應方案，並稱伊朗武裝力量的反制將比先前「12天戰爭」與「40天戰爭」更具毀滅性，「新作戰計畫不會遵循他們熟悉的規則」。
雷札伊身分相當具分量，曾任革命衛隊總司令，現掌伊朗安全決策核心機構。這一表態正值中東海域風險上升，因根據英國海上貿易行動辦公室數據，沙烏地阿拉伯朱拜勒附近海域接連有油輪遭不明發射物及火箭彈襲擊，阿曼灣、荷姆茲海峽週邊亦傳船舶受襲，船員暫報安全。
華府則同步釋放矛盾訊號。川普上周受訪時表示，不打算對伊朗使用核武器，也不預見部署美軍地面部隊，但華府仍保留常規打擊選項。
伊朗外長阿拉格齊則回應，德黑蘭不會在壓力下放棄主權權利，但仍準備對話。
分析人士認為，伊朗意在以強硬威懾換取談判籌碼，商船遇襲與荷姆茲通航風險則持續牽動能源市場神經。
paras_en: Iran’s Supreme National Security Council secretary, Rezaei, warned on Sunday (the 18th) that a response plan has been drafted for any new adventurism by the United States and Israel, and said Iran’s armed forces would retaliate with a level of devastation greater than the previous “12‑day war” and “40‑day war,” noting that the new operational plan would not follow the rules they are accustomed to.

Rezaei’s statement carries weight; he is a former commander of the Revolutionary Guard and now heads Iran’s core security‑decision body. The remark comes as risks in Middle‑East waters rise, with UK Maritime Trade Operations data showing a series of attacks on tankers near Saudi Arabia’s Jabal al‑Dukhan, as well as incidents in the Oman Sea and the Strait of Hormuz where vessels were struck by unknown projectiles and rockets, though crews have so far reported being safe.

Washington simultaneously sent mixed signals. In an interview last week, President Trump said he does not intend to use nuclear weapons against Iran and does not foresee deploying U.S. ground troops, yet the administration still retains the option of conventional strikes.
Iranian Foreign Minister Amir‑Abdollahian responded that Tehran will not relinquish its sovereign rights under pressure, but remains ready for dialogue.

Analysts believe Iran is using a hard‑line deterrent to gain bargaining chips in negotiations, and the ongoing attacks on commercial vessels and the navigation risk in the Strait of Hormuz continue to nerve the energy markets.

items.title_en: <New York Forex> US Dollar Records First Weekly Decline in Over a Month as Rate‑Hike Expectations Cool and AI Concerns Persist
paras: 美元周五(16日)走低，兌歐元與日元均創下逾1個月來首見單週貶值，反映市場對聯準會(Fed)升息的預期降溫，以及投資人對AI引發股市賣壓的疑慮持續存在。
紐約尾盤，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣的美元指數(DXY)下跌0.17%，報101.87，本週下跌約0.35%。
本週公布的消費者物價與生產者物價數據均高於預期，一度令市場感到不安。不過，聯準會官員的談話顯示，目前沒有急於進一步緊縮貨幣政策的必要，有助於穩定美國公債殖利率，也削弱了美元的支撐力道。
AI類股本週大幅下跌，壓力也蔓延至部分信用市場。由於投資人已大量押注AI供應鏈各個環節，如今開始擔心資料中心營運商可能無法及時實現獲利，進而償還債務。
StoneX全球市場研究主管Matt Weller表示，「我認為今天乃至本週最值得關注的現象，是美元與AI交易之間的緊密連動。通常科技股遭到拋售時，市場會預期美元因避險需求而走強。我們確實看到部分資金流向債券，但美元實際上卻在下跌。」
本週英鎊與瑞士法郎兌美元的升幅居前。瑞士法郎受到避險需求支撐，市場也預期，即使利率環境進一步走低，瑞士仍不太可能將政策利率降至目前零利率以下。
英鎊兌美元上漲0.31%，至1英鎊兌1.3314美元，本週累計上漲0.63%。
美元兌瑞士法郎則下跌0.25%，至0.8246瑞郎，本週累計下跌0.67%。瑞郎在過去兩個交易日累計升值逾1.4%。
芝商所（CME）FedWatch工具顯示，市場預估聯準會本月稍晚維持利率不變的機率為83%，高於一個月前的49%。
聯準會主席華許(Kevin Warsh)週五出席在曼谷舉行的國際貨幣基金（IMF）與世界銀行年度會議時，並未透露未來利率決策的線索。他表示，自己不會「預先判斷」任何一次會議的決策。
紐約梅隆銀行宏觀經濟策略師John Velis表示，「我認為，目前聯準會決策委員會內部，尤其是理事們，尚未形成足夠共識支持10月升息。不過，12月是否升息仍是未解之題，從現在到那時還有許多事情可能發生。」
歐元區財政風險仍受關注
法國財政風險仍是市場關注的背景因素。10月初，法國債務風險溢價曾大幅攀升。
歐元兌美元上漲0.08%，至1歐元兌1.1227美元。歐元週四已上漲0.56%，創下兩個月來最大單日漲幅，全週上漲約0.23%。
投資人預期，美國總統川普將避免讓中東或烏克蘭局勢進一步升級，因為更大規模的衝突可能推升通膨，進而損害他在期中選舉前的政治支持度。
美元兌日元下跌0.08%，至158.11日元。日元終止連續四週貶值走勢，本週升值0.13%。此前，伊朗衝突支撐美元走強。
近期油價上漲推升美元，同時對歐元與日元等能源進口國貨幣造成壓力。
日本銀行（BOJ）總裁植田和男(Kazuo Ueda)週五再次強調，潛在通膨率可能超越央行設定的2%目標，仍是需要留意的風險。

paras_en: The dollar fell on Friday (the 16th), with both the euro and the yen posting their first weekly depreciation in more than a month, reflecting a cooling of market expectations for further Fed rate hikes and lingering investor worries that AI is weighing on equity markets.
In the New York close, the dollar index (DXY), which tracks the greenback against six major currencies, slipped 0.17% to 101.87, down about 0.35% for the week.

Consumer price and producer price data released this week came in above expectations, briefly unsettling markets. However, comments from Fed officials indicated no urgent need for further monetary tightening, helping to stabilise US Treasury yields and weakening support for the dollar.

AI‑related stocks fell sharply this week, and the pressure spread to parts of the credit market. Investors, who have heavily bet on every link of the AI supply chain, are now worried that data‑center operators may not generate profits quickly enough to service their debt.

Matt Weller, head of global market research at StoneX, said, "I think the most noteworthy phenomenon today and this week is the tight link between the dollar and AI trading. Usually when tech stocks are sold off, the market expects the dollar to strengthen on safe‑haven demand. We did see some flows into bonds, but the dollar actually fell."

The pound and the Swiss franc posted the biggest gains against the dollar this week. The franc was supported by safe‑haven demand, and markets expect that even if rates fall further, Switzerland is unlikely to push its policy rate below the current zero‑percent level.
The pound rose 0.31% to $1.3314, up 0.63% for the week.
The dollar slipped 0.25% against the Swiss franc to 0.8246 CHF, down 0.67% for the week. The franc had appreciated more than 1.4% over the past two trading days.
CME’s FedWatch tool shows the market now assigns an 83% probability that the Fed will keep rates unchanged later this month, up from 49% a month ago.
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh attended the IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok on Friday and offered no clues about future rate decisions, saying he does not "pre‑judge" the outcome of any meeting.

John Velis, macro strategy strategist at BNY Mellon, said, "I think the Fed’s policy committee, especially the governors, have not yet reached sufficient consensus to support a rate hike in October. However, whether there will be a hike in December remains an open question, and many things could happen between now and then."
Euro‑area fiscal risks remain a focus.
Fiscal risk in France continues to be a background concern for markets, with French sovereign risk premiums spiking sharply in early October.
The euro rose 0.08% to $1.1227. It had gained 0.56% on Thursday, the biggest single‑day rise in two months, and is up about 0.23% for the week.

Investors expect that President Trump will try to avoid further escalation in the Middle East or Ukraine, as a larger conflict could push inflation higher and damage his political support ahead of the mid‑term elections.
The dollar fell 0.08% to ¥158.11, ending a four‑week streak of depreciation for the yen, which rose 0.13% this week. Previously, the Iran conflict had supported a stronger dollar.
Recent oil price gains have lifted the dollar while putting pressure on currencies of energy‑importing countries such as the euro and yen.
Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda reiterated on Friday that a potential inflation rate above the BOJ’s 2% target remains a risk to watch.
